meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you have.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever happens next, none of this goes on his record, and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote all the time. Maybe it's from a study guide or a different edition.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then what are you proposing, Hale? Whatever it is, it doesn't happen in front of his class, and I get it in writing that nothing goes on file.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Arguments change between an outline and an essay. That's the point of an outline.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything wrong. Tonight, in writing, and the line about nothing on his record goes in word for word.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Put Thursday in the email. I'll confirm with Owen against his shifts tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, with the statement that nothing goes on his record stated plainly, and the Thursday, November 12 after-school date confirmed once I have checked it with Owen. I expect it in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday after school, and she still wants your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his record; that is the fair outcome, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times and answering her pasted-draft defence, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero up front, never attacked Owen, and never leaned on the detector score.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's text arriving in two large edits just before midnight on a late October night, which landed very near that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said arguments change between an outline and an essay, answer that before moving to 4.4, for example by saying the rewrite will give Owen the chance to show the reasoning behind his new argument.
